doc.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: After college: Fred Anderson, Muhal Richard Abrams and the AACM Big Band
summary: Turning down corporate computer jobs, he worked with his father, then at Governors State met Muhal and joined the AACM Big Band while playing R&B and blues gigs.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah. At that point it’s like, now what am I going to do. I want to be a musician, I want to have a career in music. Did you have a particular goal in mind?

I don’t know, after I got through college I had met Fred Anderson and he had introduced me to Muhal Richard Abrams and Bunky Green and Rufus Reid. Because Rufus and Bunky happened to be going to school there working on their master’s degree I think at that time. And I had been offered positions by some corporations for computer work, I think IBM was one that offered me a position, and there was another one, I can’t think — if I can think of the company’s name I’ll tell you — they’d offered me a position. They were sending me American Express cards you know, the whole deal. And after I got out of school I thought, I didn’t want to go either way. So I decided to go back home and hang out with my dad and so that’s what I did. So I started just hanging out with him and going to work with him and my uncle and going to his jam sessions and doing that. And then I decided I wanted to go add to my education, so I decided to go for my master’s. So I went to Governors State University to study for my master’s degree. And while I was doing that I had met Muhal Richard Abrams and so I started playing in his band. And I started working in the AACM Big Band. And there I met people like The Art Ensemble of Chicago, Anthony Braxton and you know, the movement in that direction, and Henry Threadgill and Air. But at the same time I was working doing a lot of R&B gigs and blues gigs. I was working with J.B. Hutto and Memphis Slim and in Chicago I just sort of started falling into, between going to school and working and having these gigs. And I started working with, there was sort of a fusion band called Street Dance that I started working with with some guys.
